assumptions: Each step's identity is derived from its reaction and parameters.
limits: Compares recorded procedures, not the resulting sequences.
bio.jane/contract.question: Were these two constructs built the same way, step by step?

description: Align two constructs' build procedures step by step, in order — was this built the same way as that? Works across formats: a build received as a SnapGene binary and the same build received as an OpenCloning strategy align, because each step's identity is derived from the reaction and its parameters rather than assigned.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

against.description: File id or name of the construct to compare against, in the same project.

document.description: File id or name for THIS side. The focused document when omitted.

key.description: what to align on: `abstract` is the PROCEDURE (the command with its molecules abstracted away, so the same method on different DNA still matches); `processId` is the EXACT recorded operation, identical only when the very same step ran on the very same molecules.

name: compare_constructions

rows.description: the whole aligned history, row by row: shared, only-here, or only-there

shared.description: steps both procedures have, in the same order

similarity.description: shared steps as a percentage of the alignment
